newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: AFGHAN TALEBAN ORDERS ISLAMIC NORMS FOR SPORTSMEN.
newsitem.headline: AFGHAN TALEBAN ORDERS ISLAMIC NORMS FOR SPORTSMEN.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban movement government announced an Islamic code for sportsmen on Saturday, ordering them to grow beards and apparently banning the wearing of shorts.

The code announced over the official Kabul radio, monitored in Islamabad, also ordered sportsmen and spectators not to use tobacco products, not to clap and suspend any games during Islamic prayer times.
"All sportsmen in any field, matches, training must be in full Islamic dress and avoid un-Islamic and un-Afghan dress codes," the broadcast said.

The purist Taleban Islamic militia, which captured the capital Kabul last September and controls more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, has already banned women from working in offices and going out of their homes without wearing an all-enveloping Burqa veil. It ordered men to grow long beards.
"Hair and and beards of sportsmen must be in accordance with the Sharia (Islamic law)," Saturday's broadcast said.
It said spectators applauding sportsmen must shout the slogan "All-o-Akbar (God is great) instead of clapping.
"All games, training and matches must stop the muezzin calls for prayers and the players and spectators must offer the prayers in congregations," it said.
The prolonged civil war has destroyed much of sports facilities in Afghanistan and hundreds of athletes have fled abroad.
